memory_candidates.content: Before writing 'verification X passes' into a plan's acceptance criteria, RUN X first to capture its baseline. A repo-wide lint (check-extension-docs.sh here) was already failing at baseline on two extensions -- one of them a deployed-vs-source drift on the exact file the task was about to edit -- so a literal 'the lint passes' criterion was unachievable and would have either blocked the implementer or tempted an out-of-scope redeploy to make it green. The fix is a DELTA criterion: capture the baseline output to a file in the first phase, and make the final gate 'no failure absent from the baseline', naming the expected carried-over failures explicitly so they are not mistaken for regressions. The same discipline catches task-description verification criteria that are simply wrong (a 'grep confirms zero surviving X' criterion where an out-of-scope file legitimately retains one X: the correct assertion is exactly-one, and a zero result would itself indicate an out-of-scope edit).
